title.narrative: Power Africa: Southern Africa Energy Program (SAEP)

description.narrative: (USAID Africa Regional): The Southern Africa Energy Program (SAEP) seeks to increase electricity availability and access in Southern Africa by facilitating transactions for generation, transmission, distribution, and off-grid access projects. This activity will advance development priorities including inclusive economic growth, security, and improved health and education outcomes. The program will stimulate private sector investment in the power sector by addressing key constraints related to; 1) regulation, policy, and planning to build the enabling environment for expanded access to electricity, 2) commercial viability of electric utilities, 3) regional integration and power trading, 4) scaling up renewable energy and energy efficiency, and 5) human and institutional capacity building..SAEP works to contribute to Power Africa's continent-wide goals of increasing new power generation by 30,000 MW and increasing new connections by 60 million by 2030. Over its five-year life, SAEP is designed to meet program-specific goals to increase electricity supply and access, and will deliver:.3,000 MW of new power generation1,000 MW of new transmission capacity3 million new connectionsFY 2021 funds will be used for SAEP activities that provide technical assistance, primarily training and advice to utilities and government energy agencies on technical, regulatory and policy issues; transaction advisory services to private sector energy project developers; and sharing of knowledge across the region in technical reports and webinars..SAEP will advance democratic governance and rule of law to counter PRC influence by working with key partners to strengthen governance and advance inclusive development. Efforts include collaborating with partners in strengthening the resilience of energy sector institutions, and promoting access to information..SAEP currently provides support in Angola, Botswana, Zambia, Namibia, Malawi, Mozambique, Madagascar, South Africa, Lesotho, and Eswatini..
